recs.name: Incomplete
recs.tag: The moment the scissors tear through the dress, it is too late to regret anything.

lines.x: Monday
Agh... Look at the time... Who's knocking on my door this early in the morning...?
Coming, coming. Just a moment.
Sorry to bother you, Orchid.
You are...?
My name is Jerry. One of my... relations, is a patient aboard the ship.
Hello, Jerry. Do you need something from me?
A wedding dress! I would like to ask you to make a wedding dress! Please, I beg you!
You want me to make a wedding dress? I'm afraid you're asking the wrong person. I just edited a fashion magazine.
Besides, we'll be stopping at a city for resupplies next month. You can visit a high-end tailor shop while we're there.
But Dr. Warfarin said that Penny might not make it through the month... We probably can't wait till then.
I'm sorry to hear that. I didn't know.
I realize I probably sound pushy, but you're the only one I can turn to.
Are you really sure about this? I do know a thing or two about fashion design, but I'm not a professional designer. The wedding dress might not be exactly what you're looking for.
Besides, we don't have a very wide variety of fabric onboard. I'll be limited in what I can use to design your dress, and it may not come out looking perfect.
Right, I understand. We don't have any wild expectations. Penny and I will be more than happy just to get a decent enough wedding dress.
*Sigh*, if you really don't mind, I can help you with this.
May I see Penny, then? I need to take her measurements before I work.
Considering Penny's situation... I guess we could, if you'll just be measuring.
Will tomorrow work?
Yes. Remember to send me the room number. I'll be there at 2 P.M. sharp.
Thank you, Orchid.
Alright, now go back and stay with your fiancée.
See you tomorrow.
Tuesday
Rhodes Island Hospital Room
Alright, good job. That wraps it up with the measurements. Now, let's help you lie down. Slowly.
Thank you very much, Orchid. *Cough*. He went straight to you without telling me anything.
Don't worry about it. It's the least I can do. You're looking pretty good. I can see that he takes care of you.
Right, ever since I got sick, things have been as difficult on him as they have been on me. I know how taxing it must be to keep taking care of me like he does.
No, not at all, Penny. I'm not tired!
Jerry, could you bring me a bowl of vegetable soup from the cafeteria? I'm really craving some right now.
Yes, of course. I'll be right back!
Jerry, slow down... Uh, never mind.
Orchid, let's talk more about the wedding dress, *cough*...
Right, I brought some catalogs with me. Take a look and see if there's anything in here that you like.
They're gorgeous, and extravagant... Did you design all these?
Of course not. They're classics by famous designers from all over the world. I can make a dress for you based on these styles.
But I want to see your own designs. May I?
Sorry, Penny. Jerry might not have told you, but I was just the editor of a fashion magazine. I don't have any designs of my own to show.
But I touched the callus on your purlicue just now. Calluses this thick only come from the big scissors that tailors use.
You've got an eye for detail, Penny.
I did work in design before, but I didn't do a very good job at it. That's why I chose to leave that line of work in the end.
No way. You have very good taste.
Design calls for more than good taste.
Back when I was still in fashion school, my instructor Boyd once told me that my work lacked spirit. He suggested I find another career, said my lack of spirit would only be a waste of a life.
He didn't mean my life, but the collective lives of my customers.
He sounds like a spiteful man who can't hold his tongue. *Cough*. You shouldn't have let him get to you.
Absolutely. He's an annoying man, but he's also one of Columbia's most famous designers. I really respected him at the time.
That's why I had a breakdown. I couldn't keep at it anymore, so I submitted the paperwork to change my major to art history.
And you were really okay with that?
That's not important, Penny.
*cough*, to tell you the truth, I really am not worried about you wasting my life.
So why don't you give it a try?
*cough* *cough*...
It takes a lot more time to design a wedding dress than normal clothing. If something gets in my way, it might hold up your wedding.
I'm sorry if I'm being difficult, Orchid, but please think of it as my dying wish.
*Sigh*, fine. I'll make you a wedding dress, one for you and you alone.
So please forget what that old man said to you all those years ago, *cough*.
Alright, can we talk more tomorrow, no, the next couple of days? I need to learn more about you and your fiancé too.
Of course. There's no hurry. You... *cough* *cough*... you can come talk to me anytime.
Okay, then. I'll work on a rough design based on your specs. Once I'm done with that, I'll come talk to you before I finalize it. Try to get some rest now.
*Cough*... See you.
Alright. There's our rough design. Let's see...
*Sigh*... This girl is way too thin. She's practically a skeleton. I'll have to give her some puffier sleeves and skirt to make her look less skinny.
Oh, darling, which material should we use? Organza? Chiffon? Maybe satin...?
Inspiration... Where are you when I need you the most?
(Picks up the wooden puppets on the table and knocks them together lightly)
*Sigh*... What's your story anyway?
Wednesday
Penny and I met in Siesta. There's a really famous beach there with milk white sand. Uh, at the time, I was getting drinks for me and the boys, and my eyes landed on her when I turned around.
It was crowded, but I noticed her right away. The setting sun was slowly sinking into the sea, dying its waters yellow, and the sky...
The sky was pink. It was magnificent and beautiful. Everyone at the beach was gasping in awe or taking pictures, but not me.
I just kept looking at her.
Siesta... What is Siesta like? Maybe I should give Ceylon a call.
Hello, Ceylon? Sorry for calling you at this hour.
So, I remember you're from Siesta.
No, nothing happened. I just wanted to ask if you had any pictures or videos of the Siestan seascape that I could use as a reference.
Okay, thank you. I'll come pick it up tomorrow.
Thanks.
Thursday.
*Cough*, someone had just thrown beer in my face... I turned around and found a giddy boy giggling at me. I could only smile back awkwardly. Then... *cough*... what happened next was really weird.
He came up to me and asked if I wanted to see some hydrangeas.
*Cough*... I've had guys hit on me with worse pick-up lines, and he was stammering all the way...
Hnn—But I took him up on it.
We visited the most beautiful garden I'd ever seen. There were these small balls of flowers packed together. All of which he cared for himself... *cough*.
Up until then, I had never seen so many colorful hydrangeas.
Sorry, Lena, but would it be okay if I come pick some hydrangeas at your greenhouse this weekend?
Sorry, Orchid, but I'm running low on hydrangeas this month, and I need them for my perfumes... Mind if I ask what you need them for?
Do you know about Penny at the ICU?
She and her fiancé are getting married in her room this weekend. You know what bad shape she's in. There's only so much we can do with the venue, but I want to try to decorate it as best I can.
Oh, that girl? It's true, things aren't looking very bright for her. She might... Never mind. Can you come fetch them tomorrow?
Of course. Will eight o'clock in the evening do?
Of course. You should take care of yourself too and get some rest. You don't seem very well lately.
You're right... design work is exhausting... Anyway, thank you, Lena.
Friday
She told you about the hydrangeas, right? She probably told you about the scissors, too.
A lot of people think my hobbies, gardening and papercutting, are a little... how should I say this... unmanly, right.
But Penny doesn't think so. She actually likes them. Sometimes we sit in the garden together for a whole day just cutting a single piece of paper into different shapes.
She's very good at it. Not so clumsy like me.
Sorry, Orchid. I caught a cold a couple days ago. If it wasn't for that, I would've helped you out.
Here are the laces you asked for. I got them from back home. They're all handmade and easy on the skin. Not too prickly.
They feel very different to the touch. Thanks.
Oh, right, I have a question I want to ask you. Let's say I wanted to add some elements of papercutting to the design. How would you trim the dress?
Do you have a design drawing? Let me see...
Here you go. Thanks for your help.
Saturday
*Cough*... Jerry sold the house to pay for my treatment...
I wonder... how the garden is doing... *cough*. Without anyone taking care of the flowers, they probably all withered.
The days we spent cutting paper together... were quiet and carefree. Too bad... those days are behind us...
Back then... we would even play games... *cough*...
*Cough*... Jerry didn't know how to play very well, so I helped him...
What a dummy I was... *cough*... Who'll play with him now...?
(Why did I accept his proposal...?)
The hydrangea patch on the chest... there we go. Sew it on... perfect.
The dip dyed skirt... Hm... is this too light of a shade? Let me take a look from a little farther away.
No, this is just the right shade of blue.
Man, this skirt looks just like a hollowed-out papercutting. Bibeak's a genius.
Okay, darling... I'm quite fond of you.
I hope Penny will like you, too.
Monday
Right now, slowly...
Thank you, Orchid.
Phew... Okay. It's a good thing I made it with buttons up front instead of fastening in the back.
It's beautiful... Thank you. Just looking at it... it brings back so many memories.
(Fondles the dress feebly)
I love it... Thank you, Orchid. You seem... exhausted.
Thank you... so much.
Don't mention it. After you try it on today, I'll bring it back and work on the collar with some laces. It'll be finished soon.
Tomorrow, you'll wear it and marry Jerry.
That's great... but I'm sorry. I can't... I can't wear it.
Don't be silly. This dress was made for you and for that moment.
Tomorrow, with everyone's blessings, Jerry and you will become husband and wife while you wear this dress.
You'll have a champagne tower, a balloon arch, and cookies all day long. When everyone walks past you tomorrow, they'll gasp in admiration: Oh, what a beautiful bride.
I'm sorry, Orchid...
Right from the start, I never expected you to finish it... I thought that... I wouldn't have to turn him down again if you didn't finish.
I turned him down... so many times. I couldn't bring myself to do it again.
What you said is so beautiful... If only we could bring everything to a stop then... but I... I can't be so selfish.
I... I'm very thankful for your work, but please... please don't finish this dress. I can't marry him... I can't.
I know how you feel. All brides feel like this before a wedding.
But you can't back down in the face of those emotions. You two love each other deeply, don't you?
This isn't backing down...
Orchid... I love papercutting... but... I don't like making the final snip.
If I mess it up... It can't be fixed. If I can't bear the responsibility... then I should set the scissors down... and stop.
(Holds the girl's hands) Penny... You're wrong. You want to see it finished, don't you? If you quit now, it will never be finished.
It won't be finished, but there will still be a future. Whether it's good or bad... I don't know, but it's enough. There's still time. He can still find someone else.
Jerry will regret this the rest of his life. All because you're giving up now, Penny.
Right, it'll really weigh on him... but he won't be bound by our vows. He'll get better in the end... I hope he will.
Have you made up your mind?
Yes. Please help me. I... I can't bring myself to turn him down myself... and see him that sad.
Alright, Penny.
That night...
Darling, I have some bad news. Penny never wanted to see you finished.
Does she like you? Yes, she does. Does she want you, though? No, she doesn't.
Looks like I've wasted a lot of energy on something that I should never have gotten myself mixed up in.
I could finish you and keep you... and no one would know...
But what point is there in doing that?
Phew—
(Picks up the pair of scissors on the desk)
That's why... I'm sorry, my darling.

Under the moonlight, a cold ray of light is reflected on the pair of scissors held high. Just like a cruel, merciless bolt from the blue, it tears the beautiful wedding dress on the hanger asunder, splitting it into two halves.
I can't finish you.
Two weeks later...
No, how could you cut it up?!
I've already done it. Another glass of whisky, Joe? Thanks.
I really regretted doing this, especially when Jerry found out the next day that I didn't finish the dress.
Was he mad about it?
I wish he was, but he wasn't.
Did he say anything?
Not a thing. All he did was nod and leave.
Well, that sounds terrible.
You know what made it worse? Penny passed away on the day the wedding was supposed to be held. I didn't go to her funeral, because I didn't know if I could stand to look Jerry in the eye.
But that was over two weeks ago. Why are you here drowning your sorrows now?
Because Jerry paid me a visit this morning.
What did he say?
That he's leaving.
Before he left, he gave me a pair of scissors. He said it was a present Penny once gave him. He wanted to give them to me at the funeral, but I didn't show, and I'd been avoiding him since, so...
He had no choice but to drop in on you.
Sure enough. Hmm, this glass is all gone too. Get me another?
I think you're drinking a little too much.
You know how well I hold my liquor.
When we said our goodbyes, I tried to comfort the boy and tell him to get back on his feet. It's what Penny would've wanted.
But he said to me...
But, Orchid... When the sun sets on someone, it doesn't matter how many stars there are in the sky. They can't help him out of this long night.
That filled me with regret. I shouldn't have cut the dress up. I should've pushed Penny to go ahead with the wedding. Then maybe Jerry would've felt better.
But you didn't do that.
Because I wanted to run away, again, and Penny gave me a good excuse to do it.
The truth is, every moment I spent with Penny tormented me. I never felt so clearly just how life slips away from somebody, bit by bit.
(Trembling) It scares me... I tried to hold it in and to act normal in front of people.
But I can't help but wonder when I'm alone: What if that was me in the bed?
I have Oripathy, too!
(Holds Orchid's hand)
So, once again, I crumbled. Once again, I ran away. Once again, I didn't see things through.
Another glass for you, Orchid?
Thanks.
(Raises glass)
To Jerry and Penny, to dreams and failure, to that stinking old bastard Boyd...
To life and death.
(Finishes in a single gulp)

recs.name: The Founding of A6
recs.tag: That night, a bond was formed between the members of A6 for the first time.

lines.x: Popukar... Spot can't cover you if you're too far forward.
And you were completely out of position, Catapult.
That cover was in a lousy spot.
How was I supposed to blast those slugs if I didn't have line-of-sight?
Besides, I wouldn't have gotten jumped if Spot wasn't holed up in the back.
Me? Holed up in the back?
Open your eyes, sister. That was simulated Originium artillery.
You and Midnight would've been dust if I didn't have my shield up there.
Not that things turned out much different, in the end.
While the result was less than elegant, my magnificent swordplay brought low at least three foes before I fell.
I think there was plenty of entertainment to be had.
I'm sorry... I didn't see the one behind...
I just wanted to cut through that bad guy for Miss Orchid...
It's not about how many enemies you took out.
It's about teamwork.
We are Reserve Op Team A6.
We are a—
A motley crew of misfits.
I heard that, Catapult.
Never mind. Let's call it a day. Dismissed.
Why the long face, Orchid?
Why do you think?
Spot, Catapult, Midnight. All good people, but why can't they get along when you put them together?
Beats me. They're hardly the weirdest, by Rhodes Island standards. People generally like them.
I know.
Maybe some people just don't mix well.
Weren't the reserve op teams supposed to be experimental anyway? You could always apply for a transfer to Logistics Department.
(Mutters) But I only volunteered for the front lines because I got tired of sitting in an office pushing papers.
What was that?
You're right. When I was named captain of A6, HR told me not to feel pressure about it.
Then why do you—
Still...
Rhodes Island must have put me in charge so I can help them figure out what a team is.
Individuality is all well and good, but it must be established on the basis of mutual respect. It's not ability they're missing; it's respect for each other.
Right now, A6 isn't a team; it's just a pile of strangers tossed into the same room.
Wait a second, Orchid. There are so many bright minds on Rhodes Island; surely you don't have to be the one who has to worry about it?
It's normal for me to worry, isn't it?
I just feel like they should get to know each other, because we talk about stuff like teamwork. Not as operators, but simply knowing each other as people.
If they can establish basic social relationships, sit down and talk to each other calmly...
You've always been soft-hearted.
Let me try again.
Are you sure? You might be disappointed again.
I'm not sure I can drink this hot cocoa in peace, if I don't at least try.
That's the last card, Catapult!
No peeking at Spot's cards!

It's called tactical recon!
You have the Joker in your hand, don't you, Spot?
I can tell, the way your face froze!
That's my poker face, you idiot. Besides... I win.
Straight.
Hey! You must've cheated! How did you get so lucky?
I guess fate isn't smiling on Catapult today either.
A magnificent play by Spot, though.
Even I got fooled.
Spot's so good!
Just lucky.
Next round?
No rush. I prepared some snacks.
Mm... you really do know how to make a cup of tea, Orchid. I don't think I've had a cup this good in months.
Thanks, Midnight. By the way, these magazines are for you. I think you'll find the styles you're looking for in them.
Oh, you're too kind.
Hey, these cookies aren't bad.
Better than the ones I buy, at any rate.
I'll get more next time. You should eat more, Spot. I don't see you outside often lately.
Tea parties are kind of a bother, but I don't mind free food and drink.
They're great! You're awesome, Orchid!
Glad to see you guys looking relaxed.
We really should be able to get along with one another, shouldn't we?
If we can enjoy afternoon tea together...
I'm sure we can learn to trust each other on the battlefield.
I think... we can try to get to know each other better.
Not as operators, but as friends.
Maybe we can talk about our interests, for example?
Captain, I'll be frank with you.
What is it?
I think you're a decent person. You bought us stuff, helped us write our reports, even put together a nice tea party.
But there's a one thing that's been bugging me—why do we have to look like a team?
We're a team only because Rhodes Island happened to put us together. Sometimes a bad fit is a bad fit.
You know I'm usually on your side, Orchid.
But I have to agree with Catapult, even if her words are a little blunt.
There's no need to force things. We could be cordial colleagues, friends even. But there's no need for us to act the part of family.
It's not necessary, for you and for us.
All I can say is don't be too hard on yourself, captain.
Why did everyone go away, Miss Orchid?
Was Popukar a bad girl?
No.
You're a good girl, Popukar.
It's a bunch of grown men and women who are bad...
We screwed up.
I like summer.
The summer outfits column was one of my favorite jobs when I was still a fashion editor.
I'm not an outdoorsy or social woman, but I loved the feeling of vitality that models wearing those outfits gave off.
It's proof that someone is living a life.
And it helps me want to live mine.
How did it come to this? Maybe I should put in a transfer request with HR tomorrow.
Still...
Oh, screw it.

I'm hurting all over, and the a/c's useless. How am I supposed to get any sleep like this?
Painkillers, painkillers...
Ugh, I'm out.
Guess I need to go to the clinic.
I hate summer.
I hate that heat that engulfs my body.
And I hate how I ache when a humid breeze blows past.
The pain is almost unbearable on those wet, humid nights.
I didn't have to pass by the deck on my way to the clinic.
But I came anyway.
I wasn't sure why. Maybe it was because my body knew it wasn't painkillers that I really wanted.
There's someone on the deck, holding a bottle in his hand.
He's not wearing his signature smile, only calmness with a hint of melancholy.
...Orchid?
He tries to hide the bottle, but there is nowhere on the deck to hide it. He ends up abashedly stashing it behind his back.
I-I was just catching some fresh air—
...Are you hurting?
Yes.
Then stay put.
I'm not here to scold you.
Pour me one.
Do you drink too?
I'm not proud of it, but I do.
I hate the feeling of being drunk.
Hah, I had customers like that.
No fans of the nightlife scene, but they were forced to come by their bosses or friends.
How did you deal with them?
Get them drunk so that they'd pay you?
People who are actually drunk didn't pay all that much.
The ones who actually loosened their purse strings were the types who kept themselves bottled up, until they decideed to pour out a little bit of their true selves to a stranger under the influence.
Are you saying I'm your favorite kind of customer?
They were my friends. Best friends.
Honeyed words.
Spot can testify. I showed him some photos of me with my friends.
Am I right, Spot?
Spot?!
Just so it's clear, I was here first, then Midnight showed up second. Now you make three.
Does Oripathy give everyone a desire for fresh air at night?
Reading comics in a place like this... you'll ruin your eyes.
My vision is excellent, thank you very much.
But frankly, I like you more right now than I usually like you, Captain.
That's a brand new compliment...
Do you get together here often?
Sometimes. Spot's not exactly my type.
Total coincidence, alright? Plenty of people show up here at night, but we happen to be the only ones today—
Oh.
Miss Orchid! You're really here!
Catapult! Popukar! What are you two—
I couldn't sleep because my eye was hurting. I was looking for you but I didn't know where you were.
So I asked Catapult, and she found you, just like that?
Catapult...
(Whisper) Uh, it's not like that, Captain.
(Whisper) I was gonna take her some place I was familiar with, give her some candy, and put her to bed.
(Whisper) I had no idea all of you were here.
(Whisper) Do people really come here so often? I was just making that up!
...Now this is more like it.
What's everyone doing here?
Does your eye still hurt, Popukar?

Yeah.
But I feel better now that you're all here!
What about the rest of you?
Come now, this is not a debriefing.
I can tell you, I'm hurting like hell.
I doubt Popukar could have woken me up if I wasn't hurting.
I wouldn't be reading comics if I wasn't hurting.
I already told you.
Did anyone bring painkillers?
I brought some when I left my room. There should be enough for all of us.
You got any more drinks up your sleeves, Midnight?
Spot was actually right when he said people like to get some fresh air on deck.
That's why I've got various drinks stowed up here, just in case.
'Just in case.' Is that a synonym for 'everything'?
Everything.
Let's have a drink, then.
Here? Now?
What? Did you think I was just going to dismiss you?
Or say something that would make me want to jump off this deck, like you did earlier today.
Too tired for that.
I think I like you better when you're tired.
Then you don't know me well enough. This is how I usually am.
I only do all that stuff because I'm your captain. Can you imagine how pissed I was when you didn't respond to it?
Well, I just didn't like it.
Alright, sorry.
What?
Nothing. Just that I guess we really didn't know each other well enough.
What would you like to drink, Popukar?
Apple juice! Mr. Midnight!
Here you go.
I want gin!
Sure.
Brandy! Mr. Midnight!
You've got hands, use them.
Jerk.
I once read in a magazine—
True friendship is not about knowing what your friends like. It's about knowing what they don't like.
I have a suggestion.
Why don't we talk about our disinterests?
I'll start. I hate anything that keeps people from smiling. Illness, war, hatred, lies, cheating...
Wait a minute, the list's getting weird.
Because that's how things are. There are just so many things that can keep someone from smiling.
That's true.
Thanks. What about you, Catapult?
Oh, there are plenty of things I hate. A boring life, bad food, tedious missions. Oh, and those knights carrying their swords and shields!
How did you live for so long with so much hate in your heart?
Because I live to spite the things I hate!
Never mind me. I think you might hate even more things than I do, Spot.
No way.
Unlike you, my hatred is directed towards very specific things. Cheerful people, arrogant people, smooth-talking people, people with too much energy...
You might as well say that you hate everyone. Besides, you're obviously talking about us!
Let me finish.
You guys are a lot like the people that I hate, but I guess you're the exception that proves the rule.
Whoa, we've got a weirdo here.
You're the last person I want to hear that from.
So Spot hates everyone, except us. Does that sound better?
I think I'm already having second thoughts.
What about you, Popukar?
I... I... I hate...
Getting sleepy? Come, you can rest on my lap.
No... I wanna... hang out...
Alright, alright.
I think that's enough for tonight.
You're not running away, are you, Captain?
Are you?
It would be most dastardly.
I hate Oripathy. I hate not being able to sleep because of the pain.
I hate that I'm forced to accept all of this, when I never asked for it.
Is that why you wanted to deal with us in your own way, so that you could feel like everything's normal?
I don't know. But I assure you that I've given up on being a good captain.
I won't put what happened tonight in my reports.
I'll still give my orders in the next test, but I'll let you act as you see fit.
That's good news.
I think that's enough drinks for tonight. It's time to go to bed.
One last toast before we go?
Sure, sounds fun.
...Alright.
...You guys weren't like this earlier today.
It's a worthy night for a toast, isn't it?
To what, though?

...
To all of us hurting like hell right now.
Oh, come on, really?
But you know what? I like it.
Not bad.
It hurts like hell. But it feels better when you know there are people hurting together with you.

You know, Orchid... all those friends of mine who keep themselves bottled up, until they decide to pour out a little bit of their true selves to a stranger under the influence... they all had one thing in common.
They all thought their pain was unique, until they poured it out.
Did you really think I wouldn't get angry?
You wouldn't, because you know exactly what I'm talking about.
...It's hardly a positive thing to know that one's pain is not unique. And sharing one's pain is just that, nothing more. Bottling up isn't so bad.
Try something simpler the next time you're trying to comfort someone.
We just happened to gather here tonight because of a common reason. It doesn't mean anything.
But I wouldn't have had this drink, if not for this coincidence.
You have good taste in wine.
Thank you.
Heavies, 12 o'clock! Get on it, Spot!
I was already on my way!
Quit posing, Midnight! Are you trying to get me killed?
Patience, patience, I'm looking for an elegant angle.
You're blocking the light, Spot.
Midnight!
Enough talk! Cut inside from the left flank! Stop the two light units!
Aye-aye, Orchid-sama.
Catapult! There's a sniper behind the bunker!
Blow him to smithereens! Don't worry about the bunker!
Out of the way if you don't want to be well-done!
Catapult! You almost took out my hair with that grenade!
Well, your hair's still there, isn't it? Quit complaining!
That's more like it. Popukar! Help Spot push that big guy away!
Okay!
I won't let you hurt Mr. Spot!
(Together) Orchid!
I know! Don't rush me!
Tactical flag—
Got it!

lines.st: Congratulations, Reserve Op Team A6. You passed the test.

lines.x: I'm exhausted—!
C-? Hard work really doesn't pay, does it?
Look happier. At least you're alive.
The score was not very elegant, but I did strike the perfect pose with my last move, didn't I?
Everyone was so cool!
